physics.scenario: A flask of air, sealed and connected by a short tube to a Bourdon pressure gauge, is held in a water bath. The bath is heated in steps; at each step the student waits for the air to reach the bath temperature, then records θ and the pressure p.
principles: Pressure law: for a fixed mass of ideal gas at constant volume, p ∝ T, with T the absolute temperature (B.3)
assumptions: The air behaves as an ideal gas over this range
The volume of the flask is constant (its expansion is negligible) and no air leaks
All the air is at the bath temperature (the connecting tube holds a negligible volume)
derivation: p = p₀T/T₀ with T = θ + 273.15, so p = (p₀/T₀)θ + 273.15 p₀/T₀
p against θ is a straight line that reaches p = 0 at θ = −273.15 °C (absolute zero)

p0.note: pressure when the flask was sealed

T0.note: temperature when the flask was sealed (20 °C)

thetaAbs.note: absolute zero: the temperature at which the model pressure is zero (checked, not an input)

pressure-law.statement: p = p₀T / T₀ (p/T is constant; T in kelvin, an absolute temperature)

text.stem: A student investigates how the pressure $p$ of a fixed mass of air at constant volume depends on its temperature $T$. A sealed flask of air is held in a water bath and connected by a short tube to a Bourdon pressure gauge. The bath is heated in steps, and at each step the student waits until the reading is steady.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Show, using two rows of the table, that $p$ is not proportional to $T$.
markscheme: $\dfrac{p}{T}$ is 8.17 $\text{kPa}\,{}^{\circ}\text{C}^{-1}$ at 12.0 °C but 1.54 $\text{kPa}\,{}^{\circ}\text{C}^{-1}$ at 78.5 °C (or any two non-adjacent rows) ✓
The ratio is not constant, so $p$ is not proportional to $T$ ✓

parts.label: b
parts.question: Draw the line of best fit on the graph. Determine its gradient and its intercept on the $p$ axis.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Hence determine the temperature at which the pressure of the air would be zero, according to these data.

parts.label: d
parts.question: Draw the steepest and shallowest straight lines that pass through all the error bars. Use them to determine the absolute uncertainty in your answer to (c).
markscheme: Steepest and shallowest lines drawn through all the error bars ✓
Their temperatures at $p = 0$, found in the same way, are about −302 °C and −253 °C ✓
Uncertainty $= \dfrac{\text{difference}}{2} \approx 24\ {}^{\circ}\text{C}$ (allow values from the candidate's own lines) ✓

parts.label: e
parts.question: The accepted value of absolute zero is $−273\ {}^{\circ}\text{C}$. Calculate the percentage difference between your answer to (c) and this value. Hence discuss whether your result is consistent with the accepted value.
markscheme: This is smaller than the percentage uncertainty from (d) (about 9 %), so the result is consistent with the accepted value (award for a conclusion consistent with the candidate's own uncertainty) ✓

parts.label: f
parts.question: The flask is then placed in boiling water at 100 °C. Use your line of best fit to predict the reading of the pressure gauge.
